official.deadline_note: The Embassy's notice of 28 October 2025 required the online application and documents in the system before 14 February 2026; the Embassy then forwarded recommended applications to the China Scholarship Council from 24 February to 3 March 2026, and results were released in July-August 2026. No date for the following cycle had been published as of 10 October 2026.
official.status_note: The published 2026/2027 round closed on 14 February 2026 and admission results were available in the system in July-August 2026; as of 10 October 2026 the Embassy has announced no date for the next cycle, while its general guidance states that state-level scholarships are usually open every November and applications usually end in March.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The China Scholarship Council's Application Guide states the scholarship covers 'Tuition fees' plus a free university dormitory or accommodation subsidy, a monthly stipend and comprehensive medical insurance; the Embassy's own information page describes it as covering students' tuition, accommodation, living expenses and even international air tickets.
benefits: Full scholarship covering tuition fees, free university dormitory or accommodation subsidy, monthly stipend and comprehensive medical insurance
Stipend scale: CNY 2,500 per month for undergraduates; CNY 3,000 per month for master's students and general scholars; CNY 3,500 per month for doctoral students and senior scholars
Comprehensive medical insurance: CNY 800 per person per year (CNY 400 per person for programs lasting less than six months)
Bilateral Scholarship strand (1 place): full scholarship including international travel expenses
Unilateral Scholarship strand (3 places): full scholarship, does not include international travel expenses
Admission notice and JW201 visa form downloadable from the system once selected
eligibility: Be a citizen of a country other than the People's Republic of China, and be in good health both mentally and physically

Age and prior-degree ceilings: high school graduate under 25 for undergraduate; bachelor's degree holder under 35 for master's; master's degree holder under 40 for doctoral; high school graduate (at least) under 45 for general scholar; master's degree holder or associate professor (or above) under 50 for senior scholar
Applicants for bachelor's programs must take the China Scholastic Competency Assessment (CSCA, www.csca.cn) and upload a valid score report before the deadline
Chinese proficiency of HSK Level 3 for Chinese-taught general scholar and senior scholar programs; HSK Level 4 for Chinese-taught master's or doctoral programs
Meet the admission requirements of the applied universities in terms of academic ability, language proficiency and other relevant criteria
requirements: Contact favourite Chinese universities and obtain the Pre-Admission Documents before submitting the online application
Submit the online application and documents in the China Scholarship Council system under Bahamian Program Category A, Agency Number 0441, before the deadline; no paper material is required
Take the CSCA on December 21, 2025 or January 25, 2026 for a September 2026 intake (bachelor's applicants)
Uploaded supporting documents must be clear, authentic and valid; applicants bear the consequences caused by unclear or unidentifiable uploaded materials

Chinese Government Scholarship students are not allowed to obtain other Chinese government or university scholarships at the same time; concealment leads to disqualification and a three-year application ban
documents: Application Form for Chinese Government Scholarship (in Chinese or English)
Passport home page: clear scanned copy of an ordinary passport valid for at least 12 months from the expected start date of study
Notarized highest diploma (prospective diploma winners submit official proof of student status) and academic transcripts, with notarized Chinese or English translations if not in Chinese or English

Language qualification certificates: valid HSK score report for Chinese-taught master's, doctoral, general and senior scholar programs, or IELTS/TOEFL-type certificates for programs taught in other languages as each university requires
CSCA Score Report (bachelor's applicants) and Pre-Admission Documents issued by the universities applied to, such as a pre-admission notice or invitation letter

Study Plan or Research Proposal in Chinese or English (minimum 200 words for undergraduates, 500 for non-degree students, 800 for postgraduates); two recommendation letters from professors or associate professors for graduate or senior scholar programs; Example of Art for art or design majors; legal guardian documents in China if under 18; photocopy of the Foreigner Physical Examination Form if staying in China over 6 months; non-criminal record report issued within 6 months of submission
selection_criteria: The China Scholarship Council organizes designated universities and experts concerned to examine applicants' eligibility and academic performance before finalizing the short-list candidates
The Embassy reviews all applications and submits the recommended list to the China Scholarship Council (24 February - 3 March 2026 for the 2026/2027 round)
Only 4 places for The Bahamas in the 2026/2027 round: 1 Bilateral and 3 Unilateral, so selection is competitive among Bahamian applicants
coverage: Free university dormitory or accommodation subsidy
Monthly stipend: CNY 2,500 undergraduates; CNY 3,000 master's students and general scholars; CNY 3,500 doctoral students and senior scholars
Comprehensive medical insurance: CNY 800 per person per year (CNY 400 per person for programs lasting less than six months)
International travel expenses only for the Bilateral Scholarship strand (1 place); the Unilateral strand (3 places) excludes international travel expenses
application_method: Online application and document upload in the China Scholarship Council system at www.campuschina.org (studyinchina.csc.edu.cn), using Bahamian Program Category A, Agency Number 0441
official.application_route: Secure Pre-Admission Documents from target universities, then complete the online CGS application in the CSC system under Bahamian Program Category A (Agency Number 0441); the Embassy reviews and forwards the recommended list to the China Scholarship Council.
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must be citizens of a country other than the People's Republic of China and apply through the dispatching agency; for The Bahamas this is the Chinese Embassy under Bahamian Program Category A, Agency Number 0441.
official.international_eligibility: Open to non-Chinese citizens; Bahamian applicants apply through the Embassy's Category A route. Chinese-taught programs require HSK (Level 3 for general/senior scholars, Level 4 for master's/doctoral); programs taught in other languages require language certificates such as IELTS or TOEFL per each university's requirements.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: All fields offered by designated Chinese universities are open, including science, engineering, agriculture, medicine, economics, law, management, education, history, literature, philosophy and fine arts, among others.
official.research_requirement: A Study Plan or Research Proposal in Chinese or English is required, with a minimum of 200 words for undergraduates, 500 words for non-degree students and 800 words for postgraduates (per the Embassy's notice).
official.duration: The scholarship covers major study and Chinese language preparatory study, with language courses lasting one year; major study duration conforms to programme requirements (commonly 2-4 years undergraduate, 1-3 years master's, 2-4 years doctoral).
official.description: The Chinese Government Scholarship, set up by the Chinese government and administered by the China Scholarship Council on behalf of the Ministry of Education, supports talented students and scholars to pursue higher education or conduct research in designated Chinese universities. The Embassy of the People's Republic of China in The Bahamas offers 1 Bilateral and 3 Unilateral places for the 2026/2027 round across undergraduate, master's, doctoral, general scholar and senior scholar programmes.
official.program_type: Bilateral Scholarship (1 place) and Unilateral Scholarship (3 places), both under Bahamian Program Category A, Agency Number 0441
official.english_requirement: Applicants for programs taught in languages other than Chinese must provide relevant language proficiency certificates, such as IELTS or TOEFL score reports, in accordance with the requirements of each university; Chinese-taught master's and doctoral programs require HSK Level 4, and Chinese-taught general and senior scholar programs require HSK Level 3.

the 2027/2028 cycle deadline (no notice published as of 10 October 2026)
verification.notes: Coverage and stipend figures taken verbatim from the China Scholarship Council's official Application Guide on campuschina.org; cycle dates, places, documents and the Category A / Agency Number 0441 route taken from the Embassy's 28 October 2025 notice and 13 June 2025 information page, both fetched directly. funding_amount records the master's/general-scholar tier of the published stipend scale (CNY 2,500 undergraduate / CNY 3,000 master's and general scholar / CNY 3,500 doctoral and senior scholar per month).

applicant_utility.summary: This is the Chinese Government Scholarship run for The Bahamas through the Embassy in Nassau: four Category A places (one Bilateral place that also pays international airfare, three Unilateral places that do not) for a September intake in China. Funding covers tuition, a free dormitory or accommodation subsidy, a CNY 2,500-3,500 monthly stipend and medical insurance, so a successful applicant studies in China largely at no personal cost. The 14 February 2026 window for the 2026/2027 round has closed, so the realistic move is to prepare now for the next round the Embassy typically opens around November. The binding constraint is rarely the form itself but the paperwork: Pre-Admission Documents from your target universities must be in hand before you can submit.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Bahamian high-school leavers and degree holders inside the age ceilings who can secure pre-admission interest from Chinese universities early and are prepared to study in Chinese or in an English-taught programme backed by IELTS/TOEFL.
application_readiness_checklist: Email the international admissions offices of your target universities early to obtain a pre-admission letter or professor invitation - it is mandatory for every applicant, not a bonus
Renew your passport now if it expires within 12 months of the expected September start date
Register for the CSCA (www.csca.cn) in the December or January sitting if you are a bachelor's applicant, and confirm the required test subjects for your major with the target institution
Get your highest diploma and transcripts notarized, with notarized Chinese or English translations if they are not already in Chinese or English
Order a police clearance certificate and complete the Foreigner Physical Examination Form within six months of applying, since both go stale quickly
Draft the study plan or research proposal to the Embassy's word limits (200 undergraduate, 500 non-degree, 800 postgraduate) in Chinese or English
common_rejection_risks: Submitting without Pre-Admission Documents from the applied universities
A passport with less than 12 months validity from the expected study start date
Blurry, cropped or unidentifiable scans - the Embassy explicitly puts the consequences of poor uploads on the applicant
Missing CSCA score report (bachelor's applicants) or missing HSK report for Chinese-taught graduate programmes
Tripping an age ceiling calculated at application time (25 undergraduate, 35 master's, 40 doctoral, 45 general scholar, 50 senior scholar)
Holding another Chinese government or university scholarship, which cancels the CGS and bars reapplication for three years
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: For the three Unilateral places: international airfare to and from China, visa and residence permit fees, any accommodation beyond the free dormitory or accommodation subsidy, and personal living costs above the monthly stipend; Bilateral place holders still pay visa/residence costs and personal extras.
document_audit: Word-count conflict: the Embassy asks for 800 words for postgraduate study plans while the CSC guide says no less than 1,000 - write to the stricter figure to be safe
Notarization is explicitly required for diplomas, transcripts and any translations into Chinese or English

The Foreigner Physical Examination Form is valid for only six months and is invalid unless every listed item is covered, with the attending physician's signature, hospital stamp and a sealed photograph
Recommendation letters must come from professors or associate professors - an employer reference does not qualify
Applicants under 18 must also submit valid documents of their legal guardians in China
alerts: The 2026/2027 round closed on 14 February 2026 with results in July-August 2026; the next cycle is not yet announced, so monitor the Embassy's Notice page from around November
Only four places exist for The Bahamas, so you are effectively competing against other Bahamian applicants for the Embassy's recommendation list to CSC
Bilateral and Unilateral are distinct strands - only the single Bilateral place covers international travel, so budget airfare if you are awarded a Unilateral place
The Embassy only forwards recommended files to CSC between late February and early March, so an incomplete file can miss the internal cut even if it beats the public deadline
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Secure pre-admission documents from universities, complete the online CGS form in the CSC system under Bahamian Category A (Agency Number 0441), upload all supporting documents by the deadline; the Embassy screens and forwards the recommended list to CSC in late February/early March, universities and experts review, and results appear in the system in July-August.
